scenario: Fisheries acoustic surveys only produce reportable biomass estimates when backscatter exceeds a threshold equivalent to 5.0 t/km². Reportable estimates show a mean of 7.4 t/km² (σ=1.3 t/km²). Fisheries scientists want the true mean biomass across all surveyed transects.

data.description: Observed statistics among values exceeding the reporting threshold

values.note: Only observations above the threshold enter the record

question: (a) Assuming pelagic fish biomass follows a normal distribution with σ=1.3 t/km², solve numerically for the true population mean μ satisfying E[X | X > 5.0] = 7.4. (b) What fraction of all pelagic fish biomass events lie above the 5.0 t/km² threshold? (c) By how much (in t/km²) does the observed truncated mean overstate the true μ? (d) Explain the inferential risk of using the observed mean directly as an estimate of μ.

ground_truth.explanation: The observed mean 7.4 t/km² is E[X|X>5.0], the expectation of a truncated-normal distribution. Solving μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=7.4 numerically yields μ=7.28477 t/km². Only 96.1% of all events are recorded; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 0.11523 t/km². Using the observed mean directly as μ would lead to systematic over-estimation of the severity/magnitude of the process.

naive_answer: The true mean pelagic fish biomass is 7.4 t/km² because that is the average of all available measurements.
naive_trap: Only events above 5.0 t/km² are recorded; the observed mean is a conditional expectation E[X|X>5.0], not the population mean. It always exceeds μ whenever the threshold is binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Define α=(t−μ)/σ where t=5.0, σ=1.3. (2) Truncated-normal expectation: E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 7.4 and solve for μ via brentq on [-27.5, 7.3999]. (4) Solution: μ=7.28477 t/km². (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=Φ̄((5.0−7.28477)/1.3)=0.96058.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 7.4,1.3,5.0
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-7.28477)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.96058)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-0.11523)<0.01
